chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said:

I read the book of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) to Abu Shaybah al-Isbahani: 'I understood what you mentioned regarding your daughters, and that you do not find anyone like him, so do not look further in that regard, may Allah have mercy on you. For the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "When there comes to you one whose character and religion you are pleased with, then marry him to her. If you do not do so, there will be fitnah (trial/strife) in the earth and great corruption."'

key_terms.الْأَصْبَهَانِيِّ: the native of Isfahan (a specific identifier for the recipient)

ai.seo_question: What are the primary criteria for selecting a spouse in Shia Islam according to the Imams?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Imam’s advice to Abu Shaybah to prioritize moral and religious compatibility (kafa'ah) in marriage, reflecting the Shia emphasis on spiritual merit over tribal or economic status. The warning against withholding suitable matches underscores the practical implication that neglecting this duty can lead to significant social disorder (fitnah) and corruption within the community.
